facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old woman presented with blurry vision in her right eye for several months
3 recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis occurring during 5 months
amblyopia in the left eye
bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens
left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior
on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS without improvement on pinhole testing
Intraocular pressures were normal
Right eye showed trace conjunctival injection without definite ciliary flush, 2+ fine keratic precipitates, and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber
cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye
an epiretinal membrane in the left eye
No inflammation in the periphery was noted in either eye

The patient had 3 recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis, and the right eye showed 2+ fine keratic precipitates and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber.
The patient had amblyopia in the left eye, which is a condition that affects vision.
The left eye had an epiretinal membrane, which is a condition that affects the retina.
The patient had recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis, which is a type of uveitis.
The patient's age and the presence of cystoid macular edema suggest a possible diagnosis of age-related macular degeneration.
The patient had bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lenses, which are used to treat cataracts.
The right eye showed trace conjunctival injection, which is a symptom of conjunctivitis.
It explains the finding of decreased visual acuity without improvement on pinhole testing, which is consistent with macular edema.
